newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Regional food protection agreement delayed.
newsitem.headline: Regional food protection agreement delayed.

text.p: Farm ministers postponed on Monday agreement to extend the transitional period for imposing new rules to protect feta cheese and other regional food products from competitors using the same brand names.
EU officials said the delay was due to German problems with the legal text.

Greece and Italy said beforehand that they would vote against a Commission proposal that a five-year transitional period should apply from the date on which the regional food products are officially registered instead of from the date of publication of the regulation (2081/92) in July 1992.
The original transitional period was due to expire in July 1997 whereas the European Commission only approved in June 1996 a first list of regional food products to be protected.
EU officials said the proposal was now expected to be adopted as an "A" point at a future Farm Council.
